- When sentiment turns negative (especially after a spike), reduce forecasted price momentum; avoid over-optimistic rebounds.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below the immediate prior high.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00), model often overestimates near-term upside — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish mid-period (e.g., -1.00 after +1.00), model often fails to reverse quickly — anticipate mean reversion and reduce forecast slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days) — apply downward bias of 3–8% for final 10 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecasts with 3–5 day moving average filter.
